extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, marketers, startup founders, and communications people who write press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting and distributing press releases that journalists will 'pick up' — covering what makes a release newsworthy, how to frame it for reporters, practical usability items, and distribution tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine Newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The release must address one of these tests: affects more than your immediate customers; provides new data or insight; reflects a meaningful change in the industry; has human-interest angle; tied to current news cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these tests as a gate: if the announcement doesn't pass at least one, it is unlikely to earn pickup. Prefer specific, verifiable claims (data, trends, change metrics) and tie the story to larger trends or current events. Avoid self-serving fluff that only matters to internal stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter-Centric Framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame the release as a story angle, not an announcement — explain 'why this matters to your readers', provide pre-thought hooks for headline writers, include ready-to-use quotes, and provide data journalists can verify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think like the journalist: lead with the news peg and audience relevance. Provide a clear angle in the lede and subject line. Supply quotable, succinct comments that can be used verbatim. Avoid jargon and promotional language; show implications for readers, not just the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Easy to Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the release and materials easy for journalists to use: multimedia attached (not hidden behind a form), spokesperson available, background materials linked, pre-formatted facts and figures, and all names/titles spelled correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach high-resolution images, video, or infographics directly. Provide a media contact and confirm spokesperson availability and phone/email. Include a clear factsheet, boilerplate, and links to deeper background. Small errors (misspellings, wrong titles) erode credibility and reduce chances of pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right Distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Send to journalists who cover your beat, at the right time of day/week, with a personalized email rather than a blast; use an embargo if exclusivity is warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research reporters' beats and recent work; tailor pitches to them. Time emails for when reporters read pitches (commonly mornings mid-week). Personalization increases opens and responses. Reserve embargoes for genuinely exclusive or competitive stories and make their terms clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire Distribution Is Not Enough / Wire ≠ Pickup
rubrics_metrics.description: "Wire distribution = pickup" — False. Wire services are primarily for SEO and institutional presence; pickup usually comes from personal pitches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wire services for discoverability and archival presence, but pair them with targeted, personalized outreach. Don't assume wire placement will generate reporter interest or coverage without a compelling angle and direct pitching.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR Firm Name Is Not a Substitute for a Good Pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: "PR firms have magic relationships" — False. Firms typically have lists; the quality and angle of the pitch still matter more than the firm's name alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using an agency, ensure the pitch is targeted and the angle is strong. Review and edit agency outreach to make sure it's reporter-centric and personalized rather than list-blasty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bigger Announcement ≠ Bigger Pickup
rubrics_metrics.description: Bigger announcements do not automatically generate more pickup — smaller, well-angled stories often get more coverage than vague big-deal claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize a clear, newsworthy angle over size or hype. Reporters favor clear relevance and immediacy; a modest but timely and well-framed story can outperform a grand but unfocused announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoes Don't Guarantee Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes do not guarantee coverage; they only matter if the story is genuinely worth competing for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use embargoes strategically for exclusive or sensitive stories. If the underlying news lacks real value, an embargo will not create demand and may even harm trust if misused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit Quality Checklist (Quora Aggregate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate checklist of qualities that make a release pickup-worthy: genuinely newsworthy; pre-thought story angle; multimedia and facts pre-attached; spokesperson available; personalized distribution; tied to a broader trend or moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat this checklist as a final pre-send review: verify newsworthiness, ensure a clear story angle, attach usable assets and data, confirm spokesperson availability, and prepare targeted outreach tied to a relevant trend or timing window.
